title: AGI Watch
description: Seventy-six years of a field promising the same destination. Not a release log: only the moments that changed the answer to whether we are getting there.

eras.name: Foundations
eras.note: The question gets asked, the field gets a name, and the first schedule is set.

eras.name: Winters & Expert Systems
eras.note: Two boom-bust cycles teach the field to be embarrassed about its own predictions.

eras.name: Quiet Machine Learning
eras.note: No “AI” branding, just statistics and search beating humans one narrow game at a time.

eras.name: The Deep Learning Turn
eras.note: Learned representations beat hand-written ones, and the estimates for what is decades away start coming back badly wrong.

eras.name: Language Models Go Mainstream
eras.note: Generality starts falling out of scale rather than design — and then a chat window puts the question in everyone’s hands.

eras.name: The Gold Rush
eras.note: Every major lab ships a frontier model within months of the others, and exam scores become the currency of the claim. Those scores turn out to need reading carefully.

eras.name: Reasoning Arrives
eras.note: Capability starts coming from time spent thinking, not only from training scale — and the first “levels of AGI” framework leaks.

eras.name: The Acceleration
eras.note: Frontier capability stops being scarce. An open-weight model reaches it and is given away, which changes who the arrival question is even about.

eras.name: “The AGI Era”
eras.note: The industry starts saying the word out loud, on the record — while flagging its own model as a security risk.

milestones.title: Turing asks "can machines think?"
milestones.summary: The Imitation Game paper proposes a behavioral test for machine intelligence, before the field even has a name. Every argument on this page is downstream of it.

milestones.title: Dartmouth Workshop names the field
milestones.summary: McCarthy, Minsky, Shannon and colleagues coin "artificial intelligence" — and propose that ten people could make significant progress on language and abstraction in a single summer. The first schedule, and the first one missed.

milestones.title: ELIZA, the first chatbot
milestones.summary: Joseph Weizenbaum's pattern-matching therapist script convinces some users they're talking to something that understands them. The gap between seeming and being opens here, and never closes.

milestones.title: First AI Winter
milestones.summary: Funding collapses after symbolic AI fails to deliver on its promises; the Lighthill report guts UK research money. The field's confidence had been the loudest evidence for its timelines.

milestones.title: XCON goes into production
milestones.summary: The first commercially successful expert system starts configuring computer orders for Digital Equipment Corp, saving millions — and restarts the argument that general intelligence is a matter of enough hand-written rules.

milestones.title: Second AI Winter
milestones.summary: The market for specialized Lisp machines and expert systems collapses; "AI" becomes a word researchers avoid using. Two for two on the promises.

milestones.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
milestones.summary: IBM's chess machine defeats the reigning world champion in a full match. Chess had been the standing proxy for machine intellect; passing it moved the goalposts instead of settling anything.

milestones.title: Watson wins Jeopardy!
milestones.summary: IBM's question-answering system beats the show's two greatest champions on live television — the first time a machine handled open-domain language well enough to look general.

milestones.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet
milestones.summary: A deep convolutional network trained on GPUs blows past every prior image-recognition result. Learned representations beat hand-written rules decisively, and the field changes method.

milestones.title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
milestones.summary: DeepMind's system defeats a top Go champion at a game widely held to be decades from falling. The estimate was not wrong by a little.

milestones.title: GPT-2, held back as "too dangerous"
milestones.summary: OpenAI stages the release rather than publishing outright, citing misuse risk. The first time a lab's own capability warning was itself the announcement — a genre this page now tracks closely.

milestones.title: GPT-3 learns tasks from the prompt
milestones.summary: At 175B parameters it performs new tasks from a few examples, with no retraining. The first serious evidence that generality might fall out of scale rather than design.

milestones.title: AlphaFold2 solves protein folding
milestones.summary: Near-experimental accuracy on a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology — the strongest case on this page that a machine did novel science rather than fast lookup.

milestones.title: ChatGPT launches
milestones.summary: A chat interface on top of GPT-3.5 reaches 100 million users in two months. The capability was mostly two years old; putting it behind a text box is what made the question public.

milestones.title: "Top 10% on the bar exam"
milestones.summary: OpenAI reports GPT-4 passing a simulated bar exam in the 90th percentile, and the figure travels everywhere. A later re-analysis finds the percentile was against repeat takers who had already failed; against first-time takers it is closer to the 68th.

milestones.title: OpenAI's five levels of AGI, leaked
milestones.summary: An internal framework ranks progress from Chatbots through Reasoners, Agents, Innovators, to Organizations — the ladder this page borrows. Note that the company grading the exam also wrote it.

milestones.title: o1-preview, the first "reasoner"
milestones.summary: A model that visibly thinks step by step before answering, trading speed for deliberation. Capability starts coming from time spent at inference, not only from training scale — a second axis to grow along.

milestones.title: DeepSeek R1 rattles markets
milestones.summary: An open-weight reasoning model close to the frontier, released nearly free, wipes hundreds of billions off AI-linked stocks in a day. Frontier capability turns out not to be scarce, which changes who the arrival question is about.

milestones.title: Altman: "a couple of years away"
milestones.summary: At the India AI Impact Summit, Sam Altman says the current trajectory may put us a couple of years from early versions of true superintelligence — and that systems have gone from struggling with high-school math to doing research-level mathematics and deriving novel results in theoretical physics. He also dates a threshold: by the end of 2028, more of the world's intellectual capacity inside data centres than outside.

milestones.title: GPT-6 “Astra”: “Welcome to the AGI era”
milestones.summary: President Greg Brockman ends a closed press briefing with the line, and every headline takes it as a declaration. Pressed on whether Astra actually is AGI, the on-record answer is two hedges deep: that it is “not unreasonable to feel” we are now in that era, and that calling this the first such model is “reasonable” if you want to. The gap between the sign-off and the answer is the entry. Astra is also the first model OpenAI has flagged at a “critical” cybersecurity risk threshold.
milestones.counter: since OpenAI said “the AGI era” out loud
